items.stem: State any three features of marketing.
items.answer: Needs and wants; Creating a market offering; Customer value; Exchange mechanism
items.markingKey: Any three of: Needs and wants; Creating a market offering; Customer value; Exchange mechanism (1 mark each).

items.stem: Which of the following is true of marketing but not of selling?
items.answer: Emphasis: customer needs
items.markingKey: (d) marketing: Emphasis: customer needs. The other options describe selling.
options: Focus: transfer of title of goods
Scope: a part of the marketing process

items.stem: Explain the following functions of marketing: (i) Pricing of products (ii) Storage or warehousing.
items.answer: (i) Pricing of products: The price must suit the target market and the firm's objectives. (ii) Storage or warehousing: Goods are stored until they are needed.
items.markingKey: 2 marks each: (i) The price must suit the target market and the firm's objectives. (ii) Goods are stored until they are needed.

items.stem: Sethi Retail sorts apples into A, B and C classes by size and quality. Which function of marketing is performed?
items.answer: Standardisation and grading
items.markingKey: (d) Standardisation and grading. Grading sorts products into classes.

items.stem: Reddy Retail gives its kitchen appliances a distinctive name and logo. Which function of marketing is performed? Justify your answer.
items.answer: Branding. It gives the product an identity.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for identifying Branding; 2 marks for the justification: It gives the product an identity.

items.stem:
Thakur Agencies found that customers in Ranchi wanted low-sugar biscuits. It designed such a product, graded it by quality, and set up a helpline for complaints.
(i) Which marketing philosophy is followed? Why? (ii) Identify two functions of marketing in the case.
items.answer: (i) Marketing concept: the firm first identifies customer needs and then satisfies them. (ii) Product designing and development; standardisation and grading; customer support services (any two).
items.markingKey: 4 marks: (i) Marketing concept: the firm first identifies customer needs and then satisfies them. (ii) Product designing and development; standardisation and grading; customer support services (any two).

items.stem: Which of the following statements about marketing is correct?
items.answer: Marketing begins before production.
items.markingKey: (c) Correct: Marketing begins before production.
options: Customer value is the price charged for a product.
The product concept stresses aggressive selling.
Marketing ends with the sale of goods.

items.stem: Which of the following best describes "Brand name"?
items.answer: The part of a brand that can be spoken.
items.markingKey: (b) Brand name: The part of a brand that can be spoken.
options: Anything of value that a firm offers to customers to satisfy their needs.
The part of a brand that can be spoken.
The set of marketing tools that a firm uses to pursue its marketing objectives in the target market: product, price, place and promotion.
A name, term, sign, symbol, design or their combination used to identify the products of a seller.

items.stem: Which of the following is true of branding but not of labelling?
items.answer: Purpose: product differentiation and identity
items.markingKey: (a) branding: Purpose: product differentiation and identity. The other options describe labelling.
options: Purpose: describing the product and giving information
Legal requirement: certain information on labels is required by law
Meaning: putting identification marks and information on the package

items.stem: Which of the following statements about product, branding, packaging and labelling is NOT correct?
items.answer: The cardboard box of toothpaste is its primary package.
items.markingKey: (c) Incorrect statement: The cardboard box of toothpaste is its primary package.
options: A trademark is a legally protected brand.
Labels describe the product and specify its contents.
The cardboard box of toothpaste is its primary package.
The tube of toothpaste is its primary package.

items.stem: Newspapers and toffees bought from the nearest shop. Which type of product is it?
items.answer: Convenience product
items.markingKey: (c) Convenience product. Low-priced, bought frequently.

items.stem: Mishra Enterprises plans warehouses and transport so that stationery reaches every town in Bhopal. Which element of the marketing mix is involved? Justify your answer.
items.answer: Place. Physical distribution is a part of place.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for identifying Place; 2 marks for the justification: Physical distribution is a part of place.

items.stem: Which element of the marketing mix is involved? In each case give a reason. (i) Patel Agencies offers a discount of 10% for cash purchases of its leather bags. (ii) Patel Agencies decides the features, design and packaging of its new leather bags.
items.answer: (i) Price: Discounts are a part of pricing decisions. (ii) Product: It concerns what is offered to customers.
items.markingKey: 2 marks each (1 identification + 1 reason): (i) Price (ii) Product

items.stem:
Sharma Enterprises named its new soft drink 'Zing', short and easy to remember, put it in an attractive pack that keeps it fresh, and printed the date of manufacture and ingredients on the pack.
(i) Identify two characteristics of a good brand name shown. (ii) Identify two functions of packaging and one function of labelling.
items.answer: (i) Short; easy to pronounce and remember (also distinctive). (ii) Packaging: product protection, product promotion; labelling: describes the product and specifies its contents / information required by law.
items.markingKey: 4 marks: (i) Short; easy to pronounce and remember (also distinctive). (ii) Packaging: product protection, product promotion; labelling: describes the product and specifies its contents / information required by law.

items.stem:
Arjun is launching a new medicines through Thakur Stores. He has to decide its features and brand, the price, where to sell it, and how to make it known.
(i) Name the concept and its four elements. (ii) Explain any two elements with reference to the case.
items.answer: (i) Marketing mix: product, price, place (physical distribution) and promotion. (ii) Product: features, brand and packaging of the medicines; price: the amount charged considering cost, demand and competition; place: channels and logistics; promotion: advertising, sales promotion etc. (any two).
items.markingKey: 6 marks: (i) Marketing mix: product, price, place (physical distribution) and promotion. (ii) Product: features, brand and packaging of the medicines; price: the amount charged considering cost, demand and competition; place: channels and logistics; promotion: advertising, sales promotion etc. (any two).

items.stem: Nair Retail launches a television campaign for its footwear. Which element of the marketing mix is involved?
items.answer: Promotion
items.markingKey: (d) Promotion. It concerns communication with customers.

items.stem: State any three pricing objectives of a firm.
items.answer: Profit maximisation; Obtaining market share leadership; Surviving in a competitive market; Attaining product quality leadership
items.markingKey: Any three of: Profit maximisation; Obtaining market share leadership; Surviving in a competitive market; Attaining product quality leadership (1 mark each).

items.stem: Explain the following pricing objectives of a firm: (i) Attaining product quality leadership (ii) Profit maximisation.
items.answer: (i) Attaining product quality leadership: A higher price to cover the cost of high quality and research. (ii) Profit maximisation: Earning the highest profit, in the short or long run.
items.markingKey: 2 marks each: (i) A higher price to cover the cost of high quality and research. (ii) Earning the highest profit, in the short or long run.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): Firms are free to fix any price for every product.
Reason (R): The government may regulate the prices of essential products.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: A is false, but R is true.
items.markingKey: (d) A is false; R is true.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: Pillai Agencies raised the price of spices because of a sharp rise in the cost of raw material. Which factor affecting price determination is highlighted?
items.answer: Product cost
items.markingKey: (b) Product cost. The price must cover cost.
options: Extent of competition in the market

items.stem: Facing a slump, Iyer Retail sold its electronic goods at very low prices to clear its stock. Which pricing objective is being pursued? Justify your answer.
items.answer: Surviving in a competitive market. Low prices help the firm survive.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for identifying Surviving in a competitive market; 2 marks for the justification: Low prices help the firm survive.

items.stem:
Iyer and Sons wants to become the leading seller of leather bags in Bhopal, but the cost of raw material has risen and many rivals sell similar products.
(i) Identify three factors affecting the price of its leather bags. (ii) What price policy would you suggest?
items.answer: (i) Pricing objectives (market share leadership); product cost; extent of competition. (ii) A low (penetration) price close to cost, as competition is high and the aim is market share.
items.markingKey: 4 marks: (i) Pricing objectives (market share leadership); product cost; extent of competition. (ii) A low (penetration) price close to cost, as competition is high and the aim is market share.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about price determination is correct?
items.answer: Competition affects the price a firm can charge.
items.markingKey: (c) Correct: Competition affects the price a firm can charge.
options: Firms seeking market share usually set very high prices.
Competition has no effect on pricing.
Competition affects the price a firm can charge.
Price is not a part of the marketing mix.

items.stem: What is meant by "Physical distribution"?
items.answer: The activities involved in making goods available to customers at the right place and time.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: The activities involved in making goods available to customers at the right place and time.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): Warehousing creates time utility.
Reason (R): Goods are stored until they are needed.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
items.markingKey: (a) Both true; R explains A.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: Explain the following factors affecting the choice of channels of distribution: (i) Product-related factors (ii) Competitive factors.
items.answer: (i) Product-related factors: Perishable, technical and costly goods need short channels. (ii) Competitive factors: Firms may use the channels of competitors or avoid them.
items.markingKey: 2 marks each: (i) Perishable, technical and costly goods need short channels. (ii) Firms may use the channels of competitors or avoid them.

items.stem: Thakur Brothers sells its cars through authorised dealers who sell to customers. Which channel of distribution is used?
items.answer: One level
items.markingKey: (c) One level. Manufacturer, retailer, customer.

items.stem: Saxena Stores sells its organic food products directly to customers through its own website. Which channel of distribution is used? Justify your answer.
items.answer: Zero level. Manufacturer to customer directly.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for identifying Zero level; 2 marks for the justification: Manufacturer to customer directly.

items.stem: Gupta Industries stores rice harvested in October and sells it through the year. (i) Which component of physical distribution is highlighted? (ii) State two other features of it that would matter in this situation.
items.answer: (i) Warehousing: Storage creates time utility. (ii) Any two of: stores goods until needed; creates time utility; protects goods from damage
items.markingKey: (i) identification with reason, 2 marks; (ii) any two relevant features, 1 mark each: stores goods until needed; creates time utility; protects goods from damage

items.stem: Chopra Retail keeps enough stock of toys to meet demand without blocking too much money. (i) Which component of physical distribution is highlighted? (ii) State two other features of it that would matter in this situation.
items.answer: (i) Inventory control: The right level of stock at minimum cost. (ii) Any two of: balances customer service and cost; avoids stock-outs; avoids blocking funds in excess stock
items.markingKey: (i) identification with reason, 2 marks; (ii) any two relevant features, 1 mark each: balances customer service and cost; avoids stock-outs; avoids blocking funds in excess stock

items.stem: Menon Retail has built cold storages to keep fruit fresh until sale. (i) Which component of physical distribution is highlighted? (ii) State two other features of it that would matter in this situation.
items.answer: (i) Warehousing: Storage of perishables. (ii) Any two of: stores goods until needed; creates time utility; protects goods from damage
items.markingKey: (i) identification with reason, 2 marks; (ii) any two relevant features, 1 mark each: stores goods until needed; creates time utility; protects goods from damage

items.stem: State any three functions of public relations.
items.answer: Press relations; Product publicity; Corporate communication; Lobbying; Counselling
items.markingKey: Any three of: Press relations; Product publicity; Corporate communication; Lobbying; Counselling (1 mark each).

items.stem: State one difference between advertising and personal selling on the basis of time.
items.answer: advertising: reaches people quickly; personal selling: takes more time
items.markingKey: 1 mark: advertising: reaches people quickly; personal selling: takes more time

items.stem: Distinguish between advertising and personal selling on the basis of time, reach, cost per person and feedback.
items.answer: (i) Time: advertising: reaches people quickly; personal selling: takes more time. (ii) Reach: advertising: reaches a large number of people; personal selling: reaches a limited number of people. (iii) Cost per person: advertising: low; personal selling: high. (iv) Feedback: advertising: slow and difficult; personal selling: immediate.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for each basis: (i) Time: advertising: reaches people quickly; personal selling: takes more time. (ii) Reach: advertising: reaches a large number of people; personal selling: reaches a limited number of people. (iii) Cost per person: advertising: low; personal selling: high. (iv) Feedback: advertising: slow and difficult; personal selling: immediate.

items.stem: Thakur Brothers sells its spices at 25% below the list price this week. Which technique of sales promotion is used?
items.answer: Discount
items.markingKey: (b) Discount. Price below list price.

items.stem: Goyal Traders distributes free sachets of its new shampoo door to door. Which technique of sales promotion is used? Justify your answer.
items.answer: Sampling. Free samples to try the product.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for identifying Sampling; 2 marks for the justification: Free samples to try the product.

items.stem: Which element of the promotion mix is used? In each case give a reason. (i) Das Retail runs a television commercial for its leather bags across India. (ii) A salesperson of Das Retail visits doctors to explain the benefits of a new medicine.
items.answer: (i) Advertising: Paid, impersonal communication. (ii) Personal selling: Face-to-face oral presentation.
items.markingKey: 2 marks each (1 identification + 1 reason): (i) Advertising (ii) Personal selling

items.stem: Bansal Traders gives a free bottle of shampoo with every pack of soap. (i) Which technique of sales promotion is used? (ii) State two other features of it that would matter in this situation.
items.answer: (i) Product combinations: A gift of another product with the purchase. (ii) Any two of: adds value to the purchase; introduces the free product; encourages immediate purchase
items.markingKey: (i) identification with reason, 2 marks; (ii) any two relevant features, 1 mark each: adds value to the purchase; introduces the free product; encourages immediate purchase

items.stem:
Thakur Agencies launched a new tea. It gave free samples, put up advertisements on television, and sent salespeople to shops to explain its features.
(i) Identify the elements of the promotion mix used. (ii) State one merit and one limitation of advertising.
items.answer: (i) Sales promotion (free samples); advertising (television); personal selling (salespeople). (ii) Merit: mass reach / economy / expressiveness; limitation: less forceful / lack of feedback / inflexibility / low effectiveness.
items.markingKey: 4 marks: (i) Sales promotion (free samples); advertising (television); personal selling (salespeople). (ii) Merit: mass reach / economy / expressiveness; limitation: less forceful / lack of feedback / inflexibility / low effectiveness.

items.stem: Jain Traders distributes free sachets of its new shampoo door to door. (i) Which technique of sales promotion is used? (ii) State two other features of it that would matter in this situation.
items.answer: (i) Sampling: Free samples to try the product. (ii) Any two of: lets customers try the product; useful for new products; builds awareness
items.markingKey: (i) identification with reason, 2 marks; (ii) any two relevant features, 1 mark each: lets customers try the product; useful for new products; builds awareness

items.stem: Chopra Retail keeps enough stock of tea to meet demand without blocking too much money. (i) Which component of physical distribution is highlighted? (ii) State two other features of it that would matter in this situation.
items.answer: (i) Inventory control: The right level of stock at minimum cost. (ii) Any two of: balances customer service and cost; avoids stock-outs; avoids blocking funds in excess stock
items.markingKey: (i) identification with reason, 2 marks; (ii) any two relevant features, 1 mark each: balances customer service and cost; avoids stock-outs; avoids blocking funds in excess stock

items.stem: Sharma Enterprises sets its price to earn the highest possible profit in the long run. Which pricing objective is being pursued?
items.answer: Profit maximisation
items.markingKey: (c) Profit maximisation. Profit is the main objective.

items.stem: Thakur Traders keeps enough stock of electronic goods to meet demand without blocking too much money. (i) Which component of physical distribution is highlighted? (ii) State two other features of it that would matter in this situation.
items.answer: (i) Inventory control: The right level of stock at minimum cost. (ii) Any two of: balances customer service and cost; avoids stock-outs; avoids blocking funds in excess stock
items.markingKey: (i) identification with reason, 2 marks; (ii) any two relevant features, 1 mark each: balances customer service and cost; avoids stock-outs; avoids blocking funds in excess stock

items.stem: Which of the following statements about product, branding, packaging and labelling is correct?
items.answer: Product, price, place and promotion are the four Ps of the marketing mix.
items.markingKey: (d) Correct: Product, price, place and promotion are the four Ps of the marketing mix.
options: Packaging has no role in promotion.
Every brand is automatically a trademark.
A brand mark is the part of a brand that can be spoken.
Product, price, place and promotion are the four Ps of the marketing mix.

items.stem: Singh Traders runs a television commercial for its toys across India. Which element of the promotion mix is used?
items.answer: Advertising
items.markingKey: (b) Advertising. Paid, impersonal communication.

items.stem: Singh Traders keeps improving the quality and features of its kitchen appliances, believing a better product sells itself. Which marketing management philosophy is followed? Justify your answer.
items.answer: Product concept. Quality and features are stressed.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for identifying Product concept; 2 marks for the justification: Quality and features are stressed.

items.stem:
Mishra and Sons makes fresh dairy products in Patna and sells them through its own outlets. It keeps them in cold storage and processes online orders within an hour.

items.answer: (i) Zero level (direct); the product is perishable, so a short channel is needed. (ii) Warehousing (cold storage); order processing (online orders processed within an hour).
items.markingKey: 4 marks: (i) Zero level (direct); the product is perishable, so a short channel is needed. (ii) Warehousing (cold storage); order processing (online orders processed within an hour).

items.stem: Which of the following is true of advertising but not of personal selling?
items.answer: Form: impersonal

options: Reach: reaches a limited number of people
Flexibility: flexible message suited to each customer

items.answer: Shopping product. Customers compare before buying.

items.stem: Which marketing term is described here? "The set of actual and potential buyers of a product or service."
items.answer: Market
items.markingKey: (d) Market: The set of actual and potential buyers of a product or service.

items.stem: State one difference between branding and labelling on the basis of purpose.
items.answer: branding: product differentiation and identity; labelling: describing the product and giving information
items.markingKey: 1 mark: branding: product differentiation and identity; labelling: describing the product and giving information

items.markingKey: (i) identification with reason, 2 marks; (ii) any two relevant features, 1 mark each: balances customer service and cost; avoids stock-outs; avoids blocking funds in excess stock

items.answer: Expressiveness
